content: {"rule":"K-S2","applies":"yes","applies_why":"The judge text uses Matthew 1:16's silence on the begetter and the absence of contrary wording as the ground for UNDERDETERMINED.","verdict":"BREACH","quote":"D1 vs C3 (Matthew 1:16): UNDERDETERMINED -- the passive egennēthē states no verdict on the begetter in either direction, and the defender answered Luke 1:27, Luke 2:4 and Numbers 1:2 in [CR2] section A.3 and [CR3]; the verb change is real [L1]/[L2] but neither text's own words state the other reading's contrary.","rule_words":"That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.","room":"none","why":"The judge labels the matter UNDERDETERMINED because the passive verb states no verdict and neither text states the contrary, which is precisely the single-verse silence ground K-S2 forbids."}
